chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Al-Qāʾim will rise while there is no covenant upon his neck for anyone, nor any contract, nor any allegiance.

key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The one who rises; a title for the awaited Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.بَيْعَةٌ: An oath of allegiance or political pledge
key_terms.عُنُقِهِ: His neck; used idiomatically for being under an obligation or pledge

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean when it says al-Qāʾim عليه السلام will rise without any allegiance on his neck?
ai.summary: This hadith describes al-Qāʾim عليه السلام as rising without being bound by any prior covenant, contract, or allegiance to others. It highlights his complete independence in authority at the time of his rise and points to an eschatological dimension of leadership in Shia belief.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Al-Qaim<sup>asws</sup> would be rising and there would not be a pact for anyone upon his<sup>asws</sup> neck, nor an agreement, nor an allegiance’.
en.sarwar: 27. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “
Al-Qa’im (the one who will rise with Divine Authority) will rise and he will not be obliged to any one under any covenant, agreement or oath of allegiance.”
